mainTopic: Hidden contact, הכשר, and food that 'acts like wood'; רבי שמעון on hanging limbs
overview: The amud opens with a question on a ברייתא: flesh touches its limb only in a hidden spot, and טומאת בית הסתרים normally does not make things טמא. The answer that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר is challenged, because רבי מאיר holds this only where no הכשר is needed. רבא suggests the flesh already had הכשר. When asked why such flesh would need הכשר at all, רבא answers that while it was on the limb it 'acted like wood,' not like food. The גמרא then uses this idea of acting like wood to answer five similar cases: leaven used as a seat, a food offering to עבודה זרה, food stuck to vessels, נבלה fat on the kidney, and seeds used as a roof. In each case, someone argued the strict impurity must be only rabbinic, and the answer is that the food was acting like wood. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's line 'רבי שמעון rules it pure' and shows it refers to the first clause, about a limb hanging on a living animal. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן starts giving רבי שמעון's source: only food you can feed to others counts as 'food.' That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Hidden contact should not make the flesh impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי challenges the ברייתא: the flesh touches its source of טומאה only in a hidden place, and טומאת בית הסתרים does not make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case of impurity in a hidden place, and impurity in a hidden place does not make something impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question against the ruling of the ברייתא. The flesh should not become טמא, because the spot where it touches the limb is hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the flesh is טמא because of the limb. But the point where flesh and limb touch is inside, not visible. There is a known rule that טומאה passed through a hidden spot does not count, so the ruling looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity passed through a hidden place, meaning contact at a spot that cannot be seen
Does not make something impure
A hidden or concealed area

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a question that began just before it. The 'it' refers to the flesh touching the limb in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is impurity of a hidden place,
phrases.notes: The place where the flesh touches the limb is hidden, so the flesh would get its טומאה through a spot no one can see.

phrases.english: and impurity of a hidden place does not make impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאַת בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים הִיא, וְטוּמְאַת בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים לָא מְטַמְּיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question against the ברייתא that was raised just before this point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the flesh becomes טמא through the limb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contact between flesh and limb is in a hidden place, and the general rule is that טומאת בית הסתרים does not make things טמא.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he had the same question and asked רבי אבא בר ממל, who answered that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that טומאת בית הסתרים does make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is hard for me too. I asked רבי אבא בר ממל, and he told me: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי מאיר, who said that impurity in a hidden place does make something impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא agrees the question is strong and reports an answer he heard. The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who disagrees with the usual rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny the rule about hidden places. It says the ברייתא follows a תנא, רבי מאיר, who holds the opposite. So for him the hidden contact is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult for me as well
Whose opinion is this? A question asking which תנא a source follows
Makes something impure

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: To me too it is difficult,
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא speaking to רבי אסי, who asked the question.

phrases.english: and I asked Rabbi Abba bar Memel,
and he said to me: Whose is this?
It is Rabbi Meir,
who said: Impurity of a hidden place does make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by tying the ברייתא to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא (הא מני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to break the rule that טומאת בית הסתרים does not make things טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that טומאת בית הסתרים does make things טמא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only says this when no הכשר is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says he heard this answer many times and always rejected it, because רבי מאיר makes a distinction between טומאה that needs הכשר and טומאה that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't he say this before me many times? And I told him: רבי מאיר makes a distinction between impurity that needs הכשר and impurity that does not need הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי pushes back on the answer from step 2. He says רבי מאיר's view does not cover this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does say that hidden contact makes things טמא, but only for a טומאה that does not need הכשר. Flesh is food, and food needs הכשר before it can become טמא. So in our case even רבי מאיר should agree the hidden contact does not count, and the question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: The step that makes food able to become impure, usually by being made wet
He makes a distinction
Many times

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אסי is not saying רבי מאיר holds the usual rule. He agrees רבי מאיר says hidden contact makes things טמא, but says this only applies when no הכשר is needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question for the rest of the discussion: did the flesh in the ברייתא already have הכשר or not?

phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't it many times
phrases.notes: Now רבי אסי answers רבי זירא, and 'he' means רבי אבא בר ממל.

phrases.english: that he said it before me,
and I said to him:
Rabbi Meir distinguishes
between impurity that requires הכשר
and impurity that does not require הכשר.
phrases.notes: He means that in our case the flesh did not have הכשר, so even רבי מאיר would not call it טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 2 by limiting רבי מאיר's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי מאיר's view explains the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר only holds that טומאת בית הסתרים makes things טמא when no הכשר is needed, and flesh is food that needs הכשר.

steps.title: Maybe the flesh already had הכשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the problem is: the ברייתא may be talking about flesh that already had הכשר, so רבי מאיר's view does fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps it is talking about a case where the flesh was already given הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against רבי אסי's objection. He suggests the ברייתא is about flesh that already had הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי's problem only works if the flesh did not have הכשר. If the flesh already had הכשר, it fits the type of case where רבי מאיר says hidden contact makes things טמא. So the answer that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר works again.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? A way of saying the objection is not strong
Perhaps
Where it was already given הכשר

steps.whatToRemember: The answer that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר stands if the flesh already had הכשר. רבא's suggestion removes רבי אסי's objection.

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is where it was rendered susceptible.
phrases.notes: He means the flesh got its הכשר before it was cut off from the limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא בְּשֶׁהוּכְשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אסי's objection in step 3 and supports the answer of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אסי's objection against tying the ברייתא to רבי מאיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection assumes the flesh had no הכשר, but the ברייתא can be read as talking about flesh that already had הכשר.

steps.title: Why does the flesh need הכשר at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן challenges רבא: flesh that is part of an אבר מן החי already has the strict impurity of its limb, so why should it need הכשר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן said to רבא: Why do I need הכשר? This flesh already gives off a strict impurity because of its 'father,' the limb it came from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן attacks רבא's answer that the flesh in the ברייתא had already received הכשר. He argues that this flesh should not need הכשר in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that food which can carry a strict impurity, one that spreads even to people and vessels, does not need to be wet by liquid to become טמא. Flesh on an אבר מן החי is part of the limb, and the limb carries that strict impurity. So רבה בר רב חנן asks why רבא even needs to mention הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Food being made 'ready' to become טמא by getting wet with one of the special liquids
A strict impurity that spreads even to people and vessels
Because of its 'father,' meaning the limb that is the source of its impurity
Why do I need it? A way of saying something looks unnecessary

steps.confusionAlert: 'אָבִיו' here does not mean a parent animal. It means the 'father,' the source of impurity, which is the limb itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan said to Rava:
Why do I need it to be made susceptible to impurity?
It already imparts a severe impurity
because of its 'father'?
phrases.notes: The 'father' is the limb that the flesh is part of, which is the source of the impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי הֶכְשֵׁר, הֲרֵי מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה אַגַּב אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 4 that the ברייתא speaks of flesh that had הכשר
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the flesh needed and received הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that carries a strict impurity does not need הכשר, and flesh on an אבר מן החי carries the limb's strict impurity, so הכשר should be unnecessary

steps.title: While on the limb, the flesh acted like wood
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that while the flesh was part of the limb, it was not acting as food. It was just a part of the limb, like wood, so it still needs הכשר as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: When it served as part of the limb, it served the role of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his answer. He explains why the flesh still needs הכשר even though it was part of a strictly impure limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that strict impurity removes the need for הכשר only works when the food itself is impure as food. On the limb, the flesh's only job was to make the limb count as a limb. It worked like a piece of wood, not like food, so its impurity as food is a separate matter that still needs הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The role of wood, meaning it worked like a plain object, not as food
When it served, meaning while it was doing that job
A limb cut off a living animal, which is טמא like a carcass

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that food doing a non-food job counts as 'wood,' is the key that the גמרא uses again in the next steps.

phrases.english: He said to him:
When it served, it served the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: strict impurity removes the need for הכשר only when the item is impure as food
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The flesh's strict impurity from the limb should remove the need for הכשר
steps.terutzMaskana: On the limb the flesh acted like wood, not food, so as food it still needs הכשר

steps.title: A lump of leaven set aside as a seat is no longer food
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a teaching: a lump of hard leaven that someone set aside to sit on is cancelled. It no longer counts as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They taught that a lump of leaven that someone set aside for sitting on is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case that fits the same idea of food doing a non-food job. This line sets up אביי's argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaven was set aside to be a seat, so it is cancelled as food. The teaching does not say how this affects its impurity. That question comes up in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard lump of leaven, sourdough starter
He set it aside for a specific use
Sitting, using something as a seat
It is cancelled, it no longer counts as food

phrases.english: Abaye said: They taught:
A lump of leaven that one set aside for sitting
is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ כּוֹפֶת שְׂאוֹר שֶׁיִּחֲדָהּ לִישִׁיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel case connected to רבא's idea of food acting as 'wood'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaven set aside as a seat is cancelled and no longer counts as food

steps.title: אביי: the seat's impurity must be only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the leaven-seat's impurity is only rabbinic. If it were from the Torah, we would have food that gives off a strict impurity, which we never find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its impurity is not from the Torah. For if you think it is from the Torah, then we have found food that gives off a strict impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a conclusion from the leaven-seat case. He says its impurity as a seat can only be a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seat that a זב sat on becomes a source of strict impurity, which spreads to people and clothing. But food by itself, under Torah law, never gives off that kind of strict impurity. So if the leaven-seat were impure from the Torah, food would be giving off strict impurity, and אביי says that cannot be.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, a Torah-level law
If you would think, an opening for 'if that were true'
We have found, here meaning we would have a case that is never found
Foods

phrases.english: Its impurity is not from the Torah,
for if you would think it is from the Torah,
then we have found foods
that impart a severe impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָתָהּ לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal conclusion from the leaven-seat case of step 7
steps.raayaObject: That the leaven-seat's impurity is only rabbinic
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle that food never gives off strict impurity under Torah law

steps.title: As a seat, the leaven acted like wood
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's idea, the גמרא answers that the leaven-seat can be impure from the Torah. While it served as a seat, it acted like wood, not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it served as a seat, it served the role of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof by using the same answer רבא gave earlier. The leaven was acting as a seat, not as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's problem was that food would be giving off strict impurity. But as a seat the leaven is not acting as food at all; it is like a wooden chair. So it can be impure from the Torah, and food is still never a source of strict impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: A seat
A man with a certain discharge, who makes what he sits on strictly impure
The impurity a זב gives to something by sitting or lying on it

steps.whatToRemember: Food doing a non-food job, like flesh completing a limb or leaven used as a seat, is treated like 'wood.' Its rules come from that job, not from being food.

phrases.english: When it served, it served the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof in step 8 by applying רבא's idea from step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the leaven-seat's impurity must be rabbinic
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treated the seat as food, but as a seat it acts like wood, so no food is giving off strict impurity
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The leaven-seat can be impure from the Torah because as a seat it counts as wood, not food

steps.title: אביי quotes the rule of a food offering to idolatry
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a teaching: a food offering to עבודה זרה makes things impure through a tent (אוהל).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Sages taught that an offering of food to idolatry gives off impurity in a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a new case, just like the leaven-seat case. This sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading impurity through a tent is a very strict kind of impurity, the kind a dead body has. Here the item is food, so it looks like food carrying a strict impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to idolatry
Foods
Make things impure in a tent, meaning everything under the same roof

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Behold, they said: an offering to idolatry
made of food gives off impurity in a tent.
phrases.notes: Like a dead body, it makes everything under the same roof impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case built on the same pattern as the leaven-seat case in Steps 7–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A food offering to idolatry gives off tent-impurity.

steps.title: אביי argues this impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the offering's impurity cannot be from the Torah, or else food would carry a strict impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its impurity is not from the Torah. If you thought it was from the Torah, we would have found foods that give off a strict impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses the same argument he used for the leaven-seat. The impurity must be rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that food never carries the strict kind of impurity. Since the offering is food, אביי concludes its tent-impurity can only be a rabbinic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah
If it would enter your mind, if you would think
Strict impurity, the kind that can make people and vessels impure
We have found

phrases.english: Its impurity is not from the Torah,
for if you would think it is from the Torah,
we would have found foods that give off a strict impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָתָהּ לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the case quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The tent-impurity of a food offering to idolatry is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that food never carries strict impurity.

steps.title: The offering acted like wood, not food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that while the food served as an offering, it acted like wood, so its impurity can be from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it served as an offering, it served as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof, using רבא's idea from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the food was used as an idolatry offering, it was not acting as food at all. So the rule about food does not apply. The strict impurity can be from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Served, was used
The role of wood, acting like a non-food object

phrases.english: When it served, it served in the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that the impurity must be rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the offering counts as food. While it served as an offering, it acted like wood.

steps.title: אביי quotes the rule of food stuck to vessels
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a teaching: food that is connected to vessels is treated like the vessels themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Sages taught that foods connected to vessels are like the vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a third case of the same kind. This sets up the next argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, dough stuck to a kneading bowl counts as part of the bowl. Vessels can get a strict impurity, so this food would get a strict impurity too.

keyTerms.meaning: Foods attached or connected (to vessels)
Vessels, utensils
Are similar to, are treated like

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Behold, they said: foods that are connected
are like the vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ חִבּוּרֵי אֳכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case following the same pattern as Steps 10–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food connected to a vessel is treated like the vessel.

steps.title: אביי argues this impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי again argues that this impurity must be rabbinic, or else food would carry a strict impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their impurity is not from the Torah. If you thought it was from the Torah, we would have found food that gives off a strict impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי repeats his same argument for this new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If food stuck to a bowl could get a vessel's strict impurity from the Torah, it would break the rule that food never carries strict impurity. So אביי says the rule must be rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Their impurity
Food

phrases.english: Their impurity is not from the Torah,
for if you would think it is from the Torah,
we would have found food that gives off a strict impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָתָן לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the case in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The vessel-impurity of food connected to vessels is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that food never carries strict impurity.

steps.title: The connected food acted like wood, not food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that while the food served as part of the vessel, it acted like wood, so its impurity can be from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it served as part of the vessel, it served as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer again, using רבא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the dough was serving as part of the bowl, it was not acting as food. So getting the vessel's strict impurity does not break the rule about food.

keyTerms.meaning: While it served (in that role)

phrases.english: When it served, it served in the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that the impurity must be rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The food did not act as food while it served as part of the vessel.

steps.title: רב פפא quotes the rule of נבלה fat in villages
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא tells רבא a teaching: the fat of a נבלה in the villages needs a decision to treat it as food, and it needs הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: There is a teaching that the fat of a carcass in the villages needs a decision to use it as food, and it needs to be made able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב פפא brings a case to רבא in the same style. This sets up his argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this fat can get food-impurity, a person must decide to use it as food (מחשבה), and it must get wet (הכשר). That shows it is treated as plain food.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal that died without proper slaughter
Villages
A decision to use something as food
Making food able to become impure, by getting it wet

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
That which is taught:
the fat of a carcass in the villages
needs a decision to use it as food, and needs to be made able to become impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth case, now raised by רב פפא to רבא, following the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat of a נבלה in villages needs מחשבה and הכשר to get food-impurity.

steps.title: רב פפא argues the fat's impurity from the kidney is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that the fat's strict impurity, which comes through the kidney, must be rabbinic. Otherwise we would have food carrying a strict impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its impurity through the kidney is not from the Torah. If you thought it was from the Torah, we would have found food that gives off a strict impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא applies the same argument to the fat on the kidney.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through its connection to the kidney, the fat gives off the strict impurity of a נבלה. But Step 16 shows the same fat is treated as food. So רב פפא says that strict impurity must be only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, through its connection to
Kidney

phrases.english: its impurity through the kidney is not from the Torah,
phrases.notes: He means the strict נבלה impurity this fat has because it is attached to the kidney.

phrases.english: for if you would think it is from the Torah,
we would have found food that gives off a strict impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the case in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The fat's strict impurity through the kidney is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that food never carries strict impurity, together with the fact that this fat needs מחשבה and הכשר as food.

steps.title: The fat acted like wood while serving the kidney
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that while the fat served the kidney, it acted like wood, not food, so its strict impurity can be from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it served the kidney, it served as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer again, using רבא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the fat was serving the kidney, it was not acting as food. So its strict impurity can be from the Torah. Later, when it is treated as food, it still needs מחשבה and הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: In each of these cases, the answer is the same: while an item serves a non-food role, it acts "like wood." So it can carry a strict impurity from the Torah. Treated as food, it still needs הכשר. רב מתנה's case in steps 19–21 ends the same way.

phrases.english: When it served, it served in the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that the fat's impurity through the kidney must be rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fat was not acting as food while it served the kidney.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's "role of wood" idea answers every case brought against it.

steps.title: רב מתנה's case: a house roofed with seeds
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה quotes a teaching: if seeds are used to roof a house, they become pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: The Sages taught that if someone roofed a house with seeds, those seeds become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה brings a fifth case, just like the four before it (three from אביי, one from רב פפא). Food (here, seeds) becomes part of a building. This step sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the seeds become a roof, they are no longer treated as food. They are now part of the house. So the food impurity they had before goes away, and they now share the house's status instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeds, or plant produce
He roofed it, covering the house with a roof
They became pure

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
Behold, the Sages said:
A house that one roofed with seeds, the seeds become pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth parallel case, after אביי's three cases (steps 7-15) and רב פפא's case (steps 16-18), where food becomes part of something else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeds used as a roof stop being treated as food. They become part of the house.

steps.title: רב מתנה argues the roof's impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה argues that the house's impurity on these seeds must be rabbinic. Otherwise seeds would carry a strict impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The impurity of this roof is not from the Torah. If you thought it was from the Torah, we would find seeds that carry a strict impurity, and that can't be.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה uses the same argument as אביי and רב פפא. Food normally can't carry a strict impurity, so this impurity must be rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house can get a strict, Torah-level impurity. But seeds are food, and food only carries a light impurity. So if the seeds in the roof carried the house's strict impurity by Torah law, food would be carrying strict impurity. To avoid that, רב מתנה says it is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Not from the Torah, meaning only rabbinic
A strict, stronger level of impurity
We have found, meaning there would be an example of

phrases.english: Its impurity is not from the Torah,
phrases.notes: "Its impurity" means the strict impurity the seeds get as part of the house.

phrases.english: for if you would think it is from the Torah,
we would have found seeds
that carry a strict impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָתוֹ לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds an argument from the case in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The roof's strict impurity is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that food cannot carry a strict impurity by Torah law.

steps.title: The seeds acted like wood, not food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: while the seeds served as a roof, they acted like wood. So their impurity can be from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the seeds served as the roof, they did the job of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב מתנה's argument with the same answer it gave to each of the earlier cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that food can't carry strict impurity only applies to something acting as food. Seeds holding up a roof are working like wood, not food. So the roof can carry the house's Torah-level impurity with no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The function of wood, acting like a wooden building material
It served, or it was used

steps.whatToRemember: All five cases (steps 9, 12, 15, 18, 21) end the same way, with רבא's answer from step 6. When food is used as a seat, an idolatry offering, part of a vessel, a cover for the kidney, or a building material, it acts like wood. So it can carry a strict Torah-level impurity.

phrases.english: When it served,
it served in the role of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the argument of step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that the impurity must be rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument assumed the seeds still count as food. In the roof they act like wood.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי שמעון rules it pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון, who rules the hanging limb pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי שמעון rules it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון's words. This sets up a question about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right before this, the משנה quotes רבי מאיר. He says a limb hanging from an animal that died is impure as a limb from a living animal. Then comes רבי שמעון's short line, "he rules it pure." At first glance it seems to be arguing with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it pure

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon rules it pure.
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה. At first they seem to refer to the hanging limb in רבי מאיר's case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה's text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון rules the hanging limb or flesh pure.

steps.title: Either way, the limb should be impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. Whether or not death counts as the limb falling off, the limb should be impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem. If death counts as the limb falling off, it should be impure as a limb from a living animal. If death does not count as the limb falling off, it should be impure as a limb from a dead animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a two-sided question. Either way, it seems the limb must be impure, so how can רבי שמעון call it pure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: when the animal died, the hanging limb is treated as if it fell off while the animal was alive. Then it is a limb from a living animal, which is impure. Option two: the limb is treated as still attached when the animal died. Then it is part of a dead animal, which is also impure. Neither option leaves room for "pure."

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you want, meaning both options lead to a problem
Death counts as the limb falling off
A limb from a living animal
A limb from an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if death counts as the limb falling off,
let it be impure as a limb from a living animal;
if death does not count as the limb falling off,
let it be impure as a limb from a dead animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ: אִי מִיתָה עוֹשָׂה נִיפּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the hanging limb is pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided argument. Both ways of treating the limb at the moment of death make it impure.

steps.title: רבי שמעון is arguing on the first line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון is arguing on the first case in the משנה, about food impurity while the limb is still attached to a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is talking about the first part of the משנה. It says: a limb or flesh hanging from an animal can get food impurity while still in its place, and it needs הכשר. On that, רבי שמעון rules it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by moving רבי שמעון's words. He is not talking about the dead animal at all. He is talking about the earlier case of a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line of the משנה says hanging flesh on a living animal can get food impurity, if it was made wet first (הכשר). רבי שמעון disagrees with that line. He holds that while it is still hanging on a living animal, it can't get food impurity at all. So he never said a limb from a dead animal is pure, and the "either way" question goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: He is referring to the first clause
Hanging loosely, partly cut off but still attached
Food impurity, the lighter impurity that applies to food
In their place, while still attached to the animal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's "pure" refers to the first case in the משנה, about food impurity on a living animal. It does not refer to רבי מאיר's case of the dead animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי שמעון's line as answering the sentence right before it. The גמרא says it goes back to the first line of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is referring to the first clause:
A limb or flesh hanging from an animal
can become impure with food impurity while still in place,
and they need to be made susceptible,
phrases.notes: Food can only become impure after it gets wet. That wetting is called הכשר.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon rules them pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by changing which line רבי שמעון is responding to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the ruling to an earlier clause of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון was arguing with רבי מאיר about a limb from an animal that died.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון is arguing on the first clause. He holds that hanging flesh on a living animal can't get food impurity.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי שמעון's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי שמעון learns from the words 'food which may be eaten' that only food you can feed to others is called 'food' for impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says 'From all the food which may be eaten.' Food that you are able to feed to others is called food. Food that you are not able to feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know which case רבי שמעון is talking about, the גמרא gives his source from a פסוק. Food only counts as 'food' for impurity if it can be given to others to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'food,' but it adds 'which may be eaten.' רבי יוחנן reads this extra phrase as a limit: only food that can actually be served to others is 'food' for טומאת אוכלין. A limb hanging from a living animal cannot be served to anyone, so according to רבי שמעון it cannot become impure as food.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? The גמרא is asking for the source of a ruling
The verse in the תורה
Food which may be eaten (ויקרא 11:34)
To feed it to others
The kind of impurity that only food can receive

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי שמעון means the hanging limb is not food at all. His point is narrower: it does not count as 'food' for the laws of food impurity, because it cannot be served to others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for food impurity: whether something counts as 'food' depends on whether it can actually be given to others to eat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means רבי שמעון's ruling as explained in step 24, that hanging flesh on a living animal can't get food impurity.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"From all the food which may be eaten"
Food that you are able
to feed to others is called food;
food that you are not able to feed [to others]

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 24 showed that רבי שמעון is talking about food impurity on a limb still attached to a living animal. This step gives the פסוק that explains why such a limb is not called 'food.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only food that can be fed to others counts as 'food' for טומאת אוכלין. A limb hanging from a living animal cannot be fed to others, so רבי שמעון rules it does not receive food impurity.
